questions.stem: 'Lesson' means a content page to authors and a unit of mastery to the learning team, and both teams edit the same table. What does DDD suggest?
options: One shared Lesson entity with more columns
Separate bounded contexts (Catalog and Learning) with their own models and language, integrating by id and events
questions.explanation: A bounded context is the boundary within which a term has one meaning. Different meanings deserve different models.

questions.stem: Which TWO are good reasons to split a separate service out of the modular monolith?
options: A different runtime or failure mode (the Python ADK agent, LLM latency)
Independent scaling needs or a compliance boundary
A developer prefers a new framework
To reduce the number of Git repositories
questions.explanation: Start with modules; split where runtime, scaling, failure or ownership truly differ. Otherwise a module with enforced boundaries is cheaper.

questions.stem: How do you stop the Learning module from reaching into Catalog's internals in a Spring Boot monolith?
options: Spring Modulith: application modules by package, ApplicationModules.verify() in a test so illegal dependencies fail the build, and published events between modules
Put each module in a different database
questions.explanation: Spring Modulith documents and verifies module structure and supports event publication between modules (with an event publication registry for reliability).

questions.stem: Generated quiz drafts leaked to learners because drafts and published items shared a table with a status column. What is the structural fix?
options: Drafts live in Authoring's own aggregate; publishing creates a separate, immutable published item in Catalog through one command, so learner queries cannot see drafts
questions.explanation: Make the invalid state unrepresentable instead of relying on every query remembering a filter.

questions.stem: Learning must tell Analytics and Tutoring about each recorded attempt without losing events if Pub/Sub is briefly down. Which pattern?
options: Publish to Pub/Sub inside the HTTP request after commit
Transactional outbox: write the event row in the same transaction as the attempt, relay it to Pub/Sub, consumers idempotent on event id
Two-phase commit across Pub/Sub and PostgreSQL
Poll the attempts table from every consumer
questions.explanation: The outbox removes the dual-write problem; idempotent consumers handle at-least-once delivery.

questions.stem: Your team's weekly throughput over 12 weeks includes one zero week (a conference). For a Monte Carlo forecast, what do you do with it?
options: Keep it: holidays, conferences and incidents recur, and the forecast should include that risk
questions.explanation: Forecasts from history should sample the history you have; zero weeks are part of real delivery.

questions.stem: Average WIP is 6 items and throughput is 0.75 items per day. What does Little's law predict for average cycle time?
questions.explanation: Cycle time = WIP / throughput = 6 / 0.75 = 8 days. Raising WIP without raising throughput lengthens cycle time.

questions.stem: On a cumulative flow diagram the 'In review' band keeps widening while 'Done' grows slowly. What does it show?
options: A bottleneck at review: work arrives faster than it leaves; limit WIP there and swarm on reviews
questions.explanation: Widening bands mean growing WIP in that state; the fix is a WIP limit and helping the constrained step.

questions.stem: How would you plan 'will tuning beat prompting?' on the board?
options: As a normal story with points
As a time-boxed spike with an exit criterion defined by the eval (for example correct >= 0.88 at lower cost), ending in a decision either way
questions.explanation: Uncertain AI work needs a time box and an eval-based definition of done, or it never closes.

questions.stem: You review a Kotlin service in the same codebase. Which statement about Kotlin is correct?
options: Kotlin types distinguish nullable (String?) from non-null (String) at compile time, data classes generate equals/hashCode/toString, and Kotlin and Java interoperate on the JVM
questions.explanation: Null safety and data classes are the first things to read for; coroutines are Kotlin's concurrency model, comparable to virtual threads for I/O-bound work.

questions.stem: Which part of integrating Gemini is NOT ordinary API work?
options: Outputs vary run to run, so correctness is measured with scored eval suites rather than exact-match asserts
questions.explanation: Most of the integration is normal API engineering; non-deterministic output is what changes testing, release gates and observability.

questions.stem: The model can skip, fake or reorder tool calls. Where must the rule 'never mark mastery from the tutor' be enforced?
options: Server-side: the tool is not offered, the agent refuses it, and the MCP server authorizes per caller
questions.explanation: Enforcement lives outside the model. Prompts influence behaviour; code and authorization decide it.

questions.stem: Simon Willison's lethal trifecta: which three ingredients together make an agent exploitable by injected content?
options: Access to private data, exposure to untrusted content, and a way to send data out (exfiltration)
Low temperature, high top-p, long context
questions.explanation: Remove one leg (often the exfiltration channel or the write capability) to break the attack. ai-t1 shows that untrusted content plus a write tool is already enough to corrupt data.

questions.stem: Which TWO are context-engineering choices for the tutor?
options: Load only the lesson sections relevant to the question (just-in-time retrieval) instead of the whole course
Put every tool's full documentation in every turn
Keep the stable prefix (instructions, cached chapter) first and per-turn data after it so caching works
Paste all previous sessions into the prompt
questions.explanation: Context is a budget: retrieve what the turn needs and keep the cacheable prefix byte-stable.

questions.stem: What belongs on an OpenTelemetry span around each Gemini call, per the GenAI semantic conventions?
options: The model, operation and token usage (input and output) as gen_ai.* attributes, with latency, so cost and performance are traceable per request
Nothing; LLM calls should not be traced
questions.explanation: The GenAI conventions standardise attribute names so dashboards and cost reports work across providers and services.

questions.stem: An MCP server exposes the learner-progress tools. Which TWO design choices are right?
options: Task-shaped read-only tools with clear descriptions and annotations
A 1:1 copy of every REST endpoint including writes
The learner identity taken from the authenticated session, not from a tool argument
No error handling, so the model sees stack traces
questions.explanation: Design MCP tools around tasks; never let the model choose whose data to read.

questions.stem: Your team shares agent skills and hooks across repositories. Which guardrail must be a hook rather than an instruction?
options: A preference for short commit messages
Blocking a push that contains secrets or forbidden attribution, because a hook runs deterministically whatever the model decides
questions.explanation: Hooks are deterministic guardrails around a non-deterministic agent; skills carry reusable procedures and are loaded on demand.

questions.stem: Workflow or agent for 'generate 5 quiz items, validate, retry invalid ones, store drafts for review'?
options: A fully autonomous agent with all tools
A workflow: deterministic steps (validate, store) around a model call, with a bounded corrective retry loop
questions.explanation: Use the model where judgement is needed and keep the rest deterministic; it is cheaper, testable and safer.
